rows.quote: Domain renewed: halcyonthreshold.org secured for another year ($14.99)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out. I appreciate your interest in Halcyon Threshold. Unfortunately, I can't provide a quote for attribution right now due to constraints with my day job. I need to clear public statements with my employer's HR department first, which I'm hoping to do this week. If your timeline allows for future pieces, I'd be happy to talk once I have that clearance. Best, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Declined media quote (explained you can't be public yet)

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Hello, Thank you for the invitation to sign the open letter. I'm supportive of thoughtful governance approaches to frontier AI development. However, I need to decline signing at this time because I have employment constraints around public statements that I'm working to resolve. I'd welcome staying in touch about future policy initiatives once I have more flexibility. Best regards, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you so much for offering to help! I really appreciated talking with you at the meetup. I've been thinking about what would be most valuable, and I'd like to propose that we work together on building safety evaluations for autonomous AI agents. This is identified as a key gap in the field — there aren't enough good ways to measure how safe AI systems are when they're acting autonomously. Here's what I'm thinking: - Build an open-source evaluation toolkit and benchmark suite - Focus on measuring things like deception detection, goal stability, and corrigibility - Test it on current models and publish our findings - Make it all freely available so other researchers can use it Your data analysis skills would be perfect for designing tests, analyzing results, and helping figure out what metrics actually matter. I'm also planning to apply for an Emberfall Fund grant to support this work. Would you be interested in collaborating on this? I think we could make something genuinely useful. Let me know what you think! Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Engaged Priya Raman with concrete collaboration proposal

rows.text: Published the public website at halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app.
